# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: AC2 drift hole — the build scripts still run plain `flutter pub get` (no `--enforce-lockfile`)**

The workflow YAML steps are all converted, but the packaging scripts they invoke resolve flutter_app deps themselves, outside the guard test's reach (it only parses workflow `run` steps):

- `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:68` — `( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null && ... )`
- `scripts/build_office_addin.sh:54` — `( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null && ... )`

Both scripts run in CI (`browser-ext.yml`, `build-macos.yml:927`, `office-addin.yml:101`, `pages.yml`). The awkward case is **build-macos.yml's release job** (`if: inputs.create_release == 'true'`): it only does root + `browser_ext/dart` pub-gets before `bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app`, so the script's plain `flutter pub get` is the *only* flutter_app resolution in that job. On a pubspec/lockfile skew it would silently regenerate the lockfile and produce a **green release build with floated deps** — precisely the drift class AC2 exists to turn into a hard failure.

Here the preceding `--enforce-lockfile` step masks the script's plain resolve (pub is already satisfied, so it's a no-op), but the hole is real on the release path.

**Fix**: add `--enforce-lockfile` to both script invocations:

```bash
( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile >/dev/null && ... )
```

(Local/dev runs of the scripts keep working as long as the committed lockfile is in sync, which the guard test now enforces.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: deduplicate the root .gitignore's doubled block**

The root `.gitignore` contains its first ~80 lines twice (pre-existing on main — this PR correctly patched *both* copies of the wasm_run block and placed `!flutter_app/pubspec.lock` after the second `pubspec.lock` rule, which is what makes it work under last-match-wins).

Placement is verified correct (`git check-ignore flutter_app/pubspec.lock` → not ignored; guard test passes), but the file's own new comment — *"Must stay after EVERY `pubspec.lock` rule above"* — is only true because the duplication happens to keep both rules above the negation. It's fragile: anyone deduplicating the file, or appending a new `pubspec.lock` rule at the bottom, silently re-breaks the app lockfile's tracking.

Follow-up: collapse the duplicated block into one (pure deletion, no behavior change), keeping the negation after the single remaining `pubspec.lock` rule.

💡 **SUGGESTION: don't retry deterministic `--enforce-lockfile` skew failures**

The retry loop exists for transient runner/network failures against pub.dev — but a pubspec/lockfile skew (the exact failure this PR wants to be loud) is deterministic: attempt 2 and 3 will fail identically, costing ~30s per red leg and emitting a misleading "network unhealthy" error for what is actually a lockfile-regeneration requirement.

Consider failing fast on the skew signature, e.g. gate the retry on the failure not matching `Unable to satisfy .* using .*pubspec.lock`, or run one unretried `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` before the loop. Minor — the loop still ends red either way.

# gh-1265: [BUG] nightly red 5 nights: native desktop builds broken by a TRANSITIVE flutter_inappwebview nobody declares — linux WPE missing + windows MSVC 14.51 STL1011 (lockfile not committed)

## Description

**Evidence** (nightly run 37260378075, red every night 10-01 → 10-05):
- Build linux (release): `flutter_inappwebview_linux/linux/CMakeLists.txt:63: WPE WebKit not found. Please install libwpewebkit-1.0-dev`
- Build windows (release): `MSVC 14.51 (VS 18) include/experimental/coroutine(37,1): error C2338 STL1011: The /await…` from `flutter_inappwebview_windows` sources (legacy coroutine-TS header rejected by the runner image's new toolchain).

**Root cause (verified on origin/main): NO pubspec or committed lockfile mentions flutter_inappwebview, and zero Dart code references it** — it arrives as a fresh TRANSITIVE resolution on CI: flutter_app/pubspec.lock is not committed, so nightly's `pub get` floats to the latest compatible versions; some caret dep released in the last ~5 days now pulls flutter_inappwebview, and its native legs break both desktop builds (linux: new system-lib requirement; windows: plugin code incompatible with the updated MSVC).

**Fix (layered):**
1. **Commit flutter_app/pubspec.lock** (app, not library — lockfile belongs in git) so CI builds are reproducible and transitive drift surfaces as a deliberate PR diff, not a 5-red-nights mystery. REG: CI fails if pubspec.yaml and the committed lockfile disagree (`pub get --enforce-lockfile` or a dry-run diff step).
2. Name the exact parent dep that newly pulls flutter_inappwebview (`dart pub deps` on a fresh resolve vs the last green nightly) and constrain it (pin upper bound) — or, if the plugin is genuinely unneeded, exclude it at the source.
3. Decide policy for the plugin's native legs regardless: linux leg either installs libwpewebkit-1.0-dev in the workflow or drops the plugin; windows leg either pins the older toolset or bumps to an inappwebview version with cppwinrt coroutines.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: nightly linux + windows release builds green.
- AC2: flutter_app/pubspec.lock committed and enforced in CI (AC of the REG guard).
- AC3: the parent dep + the version that introduced the drift is named in this issue (data, not vibes).

# Rework — gh-1265 (PR #1268): red Quality gate on head `a702c3170`

## Issues/Notes

- **CI failure (Quality gate)**: the aggregate Quality gate went red on head `a702c3170dde9b168e645a57e1cf6b9eb68869fc`. The full CI log was not attached (`ci_failures_full.log` missing), so the failing leg was identified by local reproduction.
- **Root cause (reproduced locally)**: merge commit `a702c3170` brought `chore(release): v1.0.513` in from `main`, bumping the root `pubspec.yaml` (and `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) to `1.0.513` — but the **committed `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` still recorded the `flutter_agent_harness` path dependency at `1.0.511`**. Every `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` step this PR added then exits 1:

  ```text
  Would change 1 dependency.
  Unable to satisfy `pubspec.yaml` using `pubspec.lock`.
  ```

  The first flutter_app pub-get step in any CI leg (e.g. `static`, `flutter-analyze`, `flutter-tests`, …) fails → aggregate Quality gate fails. This is exactly the skew class the PR's own AC2 REG guard was designed to catch — the merge from `main` introduced it after the lockfile was committed.
- **Not a previous-attempt repeat**: this is a new failure mode (lockfile/pubspec version skew from the main merge), not the nightly desktop legs the PR originally fixed — those remain green locally (guard test AC1/AC3 pass, linux release build verified in the PR).

## Approach

TDD (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR) against the concrete CI failure:

1. **RED** — added a test to `test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` (AC2 group): the committed lockfile's recorded root-package version must equal `pubspec.yaml`'s version, and `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`'s version must not lag the root version. With the stale lockfile restored this fails exactly as CI did: `Expected: 1.0.513 / Actual: 1.0.511` (13 passed, 1 failed).
2. **GREEN** — regenerated the lockfile (`cd flutter_app && flutter pub get`; single-line change `1.0.511` → `1.0.513` for the path dep). `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` now succeeds and the guard test passes **14/14**.
3. **REFACTOR** — none needed; the fix is one lockfile line plus the regression test.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` | Regenerated: `flutter_agent_harness` path dep `1.0.511` → `1.0.513` (sync with the v1.0.513 release bump from main). |
| `test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` | New AC2 test `lockfile is in sync with the current package versions` — fails if a future merge/release chore bumps versions without regenerating the committed lockfile, so this breaks locally instead of red-lighting every CI leg. |

(Committed as `0aff6c34e` — new head for validation.)

## Test Coverage

- **Guard test**: `dart test test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` → **14/14 pass** (was 13/14 RED before the lockfile regen). `dart analyze` on the file: no issues.
- **Enforce-lockfile verification**: `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile --directory=flutter_app` now succeeds (exits 0); previously exited 1 with "Unable to satisfy pubspec.yaml using pubspec.lock".
- **Skew sweep**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` is the only committed lockfile in the repo (`git ls-files`), so no other lockfile can carry the same skew; all remaining `flutter pub get` occurrences in workflows are either `--enforce-lockfile` or non-flutter_app library steps (left as-is intentionally).
- **Full suite**: `dart test` ran to completion with all tests passing, but the Dart VM hit a **pre-existing native shutdown crash in this sandbox** (`tcache_thread_shutdown(): unaligned tcache chunk detected / Aborted`) *after* the final test — reproduced with a minimal subset (`dart test test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_attach_test.dart test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` → "🎉 22 tests passed" then the same abort at VM exit). The crash is environmental (VM shutdown), unrelated to this change, which touches zero runtime code (one lockfile version line + a text/YAML guard test).

## Notes

- The open PR "thread" is a top-level bot comment (`threadId`/`rootCommentId` are `null` in `pr_discussions_raw.json`), not an inline review thread — no threaded replies are required (`outputs/review_replies.json` is `{ "replies": [] }`).
- AC1 (windows leg) remains verified by symmetry as stated in the PR description — no Windows host available; the stub mechanism is proven on linux.

# --- Vendored interpreter runtimes for the run_script tool (offscreen
# document). Extension CSP forbids remote scripts — these ship in-bundle. ---
"$(dirname "$0")/vendor_interpreters.sh"

# --- Embedded agent (dart2js). Output is a build artifact: never committed. ---
agent_js=browser_ext/sw/agent.js
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "building embedded agent (dart2js)…"
  ( cd browser_ext/dart \
    && dart pub get >/dev/null \
    && dart compile js -O2 -o ../sw/agent.js agent_main.dart )
  rm -f "${agent_js}.deps" "${agent_js}.map"
elif [ -f "$agent_js" ]; then
  echo "dart SDK not found — shipping prebuilt $agent_js"
else
  echo "WARNING: no dart SDK and no prebuilt sw/agent.js — scaffold-only zip (embedded agent disabled)"
fi

# --- Optional fa web app (flutter_app → browser_ext/app). Build artifact. ---
if [ "$with_app" -eq 1 ]; then
  if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: --with-app passed but flutter is not installed — cannot build browser_ext/app/" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
  # --base-href MUST match the panel-relative location: panel.js resolves
  # 'app/index.html' against panel/panel.html, so the bundle lives at
  # browser_ext/panel/app/ (a root-level copy is invisible to the panel).
  ( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null
    # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (pubspec.yaml),
    # so the web build dies bundling it when the file is absent (#140).
    # Create it AFTER pub get — pub get removes a placeholder touched
    # earlier (runs 34593431895, 34596707238) — and keep it non-empty:
    # the populated placeholder is the shape build-macos.yml's app job
    # has shipped green. A real local .env (developer keys) is never
    # overwritten.
----
# --- 3. The fa web app (flutter_app → outlook/app) — MANDATORY. ---
if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: flutter is not installed — cannot build outlook/app/" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
# --base-href MUST match the taskpane URL: the pane opens
# /outlook/app/index.html directly (manifest 1.2.0.0), so the bundle
# lives at build/pages/root/outlook/app/.
( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null && \
  FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/ \
  flutter build web --release --pwa-strategy=none --base-href=/outlook/app/ \
    --dart-define=FA_HOST=office )
rm -rf "$out/app"
mkdir -p "$out/app"
cp -R flutter_app/build/web/. "$out/app/"
# Vendored WASI interpreter assets are mobile-only (#1096 AC3): loaded
# exclusively through WasiSandboxShell (env_factory_io.dart — Android/iOS);
# the web pane compiles env_factory_stub (wasm_run needs dart:ffi) and
# runs python/js/sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net (web_interpreters_web.dart).
# ~47MB that never loads in the browser — drop from the bundle.

Replaces the hosted `flutter_inappwebview_linux` (0.1.0-beta.1) via
`dependency_overrides` in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`.

- **What this is**: a same-name, same-version stub with an empty Dart lib
  and **no `flutter: plugin:` section**.
- **Why**: the umbrella `flutter_inappwebview: 6.2.0-beta.3` (direct dep
  since gh-1235) pulls this implementation into every linux build, and its
  native CMake hard-requires the WPE WebKit system library
  (`CMakeLists.txt:63` — nightly linux release leg red 5 nights,
  10-01 → 10-05). `libwpewebkit-1.0-dev` does not exist on Ubuntu 24.04
  (noble; verified against packages.ubuntu.com — jammy-only), so the
  plugin cannot be built on `ubuntu-latest` at all.
- **Why it's safe**: the app never uses flutter_inappwebview on Linux —
  `createFaWebViewHost()` returns null there (renderer placeholder). With
  no plugin registration, `flutter build linux --release` compiles none of
  the plugin's C++ and the app is functionally unchanged.
- **Dropping the stub**: delete the `dependency_overrides` entry in
  flutter_app/pubspec.yaml and this directory, then regenerate
  flutter_app/pubspec.lock — but only once the linux leg can satisfy the
  WPE WebKit requirement (new runner image, upstream making the dependency
  optional, or upstream shipping a linux impl without it).

With `channel: stable`, when a new Flutter stable releases with a higher Dart SDK, `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` checks lockfile SDK constraints: the lockfile sdks section records the lower bounds. Enforce-lockfile fails if "the current Dart/Flutter SDK doesn't satisfy the lockfile's sdk constraints"? Actually the sdks section in the lockfile records the constraints derived at resolution time, not upper bounds. A newer SDK satisfies `>=3.13.0 <4.0.0` fine. But there's a nuance: if the new Flutter stable bumps packages' SDK constraints such that the locked versions no longer satisfy... enforce-lockfile only checks that resolution from the lockfile is still valid, not that it's the latest. Locked versions remain valid if their SDK constraints are satisfied by the new SDK — newer SDK satisfies old constraints. It doesn't fail merely because newer package versions exist. However, if a dependency requires an upper bound like `<3.14.0`... unlikely. So mostly OK.

Bigger question: does `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` fail when the Flutter SDK version differs from the one that generated the lockfile? No — it fails only if the lockfile is not consistent with pubspec.yaml. SDK constraints recorded in the lockfile are minimum bounds; a newer stable satisfies them. So stable-floating workflows are fine unless a new stable breaks a locked package's environment (then that would be a genuine issue to catch anyway... actually it would fail the build, which is arguably good — pin the SDK).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

**Summary**: Solid, well-evidenced fix for gh-1265 — the stub-override mechanism is verified end-to-end locally (`flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` exits 0 on the current head, guard test 14/14, umbrella warning is the documented benign one), AC1–AC3 are all pinned in code, and the rework correctly closed the v1.0.513 lockfile-skew red with a regression test. No blocking findings.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ AC2 hole: `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:68` / `scripts/build_office_addin.sh:54` still run plain `flutter pub get`; the build-macos release job invokes the script with *no* preceding enforce step, so a skew would silently float on the release path (guard test can't see inside scripts).
- 💡 `.gitignore`'s doubled block makes the `!flutter_app/pubspec.lock` placement fragile — dedupe as follow-up.
- 💡 build-mobile.yml's retry loop retries deterministic lockfile-skew failures (~30s wasted per red leg).

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `--enforce-lockfile` to the two build scripts' flutter_app pub-get (one-liner each).
2. Optional follow-ups: dedupe `.gitignore`; fail fast on skew in the retry loop.
3. Note: head `0aff6c34e` went red before the last main merge with no CI log attached; current head `58455cc24` verifies green locally — first nightly run should confirm AC1 on the windows leg (verified by symmetry only).

## PR Description

## gh-1265 — nightly linux/windows release legs red: unused `flutter_inappwebview` desktop impls + uncommitted lockfile

### Root Cause
- gh-1235's **direct** `flutter_inappwebview: ^6.2.0-beta.3` dep pulls the umbrella's desktop implementations (`flutter_inappwebview_linux 0.1.0-beta.1`, `flutter_inappwebview_windows 0.7.0-beta.3`) into every native desktop build — the ticket's "transitive, nobody declares it" theory is stale (verified: `js_widget_runtime`, hosted 0.4.155 AND git bd1e7c2, declares no inappwebview; the umbrella is the only graph edge).
- Linux: the plugin's CMake hard-requires WPE WebKit; `libwpewebkit-1.0-dev` **does not exist on Ubuntu 24.04** (jammy-only, verified) — reproduced locally: `flutter build linux --release` → the exact `CMakeLists.txt:63` error.
- Windows: plugin C++17 sources (no `/await`) include `<experimental/coroutine>` via cppwinrt → MSVC 14.51 STL1011; no published version fixes it.
- The app never uses the plugin on Linux/Windows (`createFaWebViewHost()` returns null there → placeholder), and `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` was gitignored, so the drift hit CI as a 5-night mystery.

### Fix
- `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` + `vendor/flutter_inappwebview_{linux,windows}_stub/`: same-name stub overrides with **no** `flutter: plugin:` section (mirrors the existing `vendor/flutter_inappwebview_macos` pattern) — desktop builds compile zero inappwebview C++; `VENDORED.md` documents drop conditions.
- `.gitignore`: `!flutter_app/pubspec.lock` negation (after every `pubspec.lock` rule — the file has a duplicated block); `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` committed (umbrella 6.2.0-beta.3 pinned).
- All 7 workflows' flutter_app pub-get steps → `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` (ci, nightly, build-mobile, build-macos, browser-ext, office-addin, pages) — skew now fails CI instead of floating.
- Stale pubspec comments updated; `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/linux/wasm_run-*/` gitignored (linux-build download cache swept into the branch during verification, removed).

### Test Coverage
- **RED**: `test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` — 12 of 13 failed before the fix (13/13 pass after): lockfile committed/not-ignored, per-workflow enforce-lockfile, stub overrides carry no plugin section, drift chain pinned (AC3 data in code), nightly still exercises linux+windows.
- Local: linux repro (WPE error) → green `flutter build linux --release` with stubs, bundle contains no inappwebview native lib; `--enforce-lockfile` passes in sync and exits 1 on skew.
- Full suite: **9013 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures**; `dart analyze` clean (pre-existing infos only).

### Notes
- **AC3**: parent dep = `flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 (direct, gh-1235) → `_linux 0.1.0-beta.1` (new WPE system-lib requirement) + `_windows 0.7.0-beta.3` (C++17-without-/await sources).
- **Windows leg** (AC1) is verified by symmetry, not executed: no Windows host available. The stub removes the plugin from the windows build graph (registrant regenerated, CMake plugin list updated — same mechanism proven on linux), returning the leg to the exact native surface it had when green on 09-30. First nightly run should confirm.
- `flutter pub get` prints a benign warning that the umbrella's `default_package` refs are "not a plugin package" — expected, that is the stub doing its job.
- The windows runner stays `windows-latest` (no toolset pin needed once the plugin C++ is out of the build).

# gh-1265: [BUG] nightly red 5 nights: native desktop builds broken by a TRANSITIVE flutter_inappwebview nobody declares — linux WPE missing + windows MSVC 14.51 STL1011 (lockfile not committed)

## Description

**Evidence** (nightly run 37260378075, red every night 10-01 → 10-05):
- Build linux (release): `flutter_inappwebview_linux/linux/CMakeLists.txt:63: WPE WebKit not found. Please install libwpewebkit-1.0-dev`
- Build windows (release): `MSVC 14.51 (VS 18) include/experimental/coroutine(37,1): error C2338 STL1011: The /await…` from `flutter_inappwebview_windows` sources (legacy coroutine-TS header rejected by the runner image's new toolchain).

**Root cause (verified on origin/main): NO pubspec or committed lockfile mentions flutter_inappwebview, and zero Dart code references it** — it arrives as a fresh TRANSITIVE resolution on CI: flutter_app/pubspec.lock is not committed, so nightly's `pub get` floats to the latest compatible versions; some caret dep released in the last ~5 days now pulls flutter_inappwebview, and its native legs break both desktop builds (linux: new system-lib requirement; windows: plugin code incompatible with the updated MSVC).

**Fix (layered):**
1. **Commit flutter_app/pubspec.lock** (app, not library — lockfile belongs in git) so CI builds are reproducible and transitive drift surfaces as a deliberate PR diff, not a 5-red-nights mystery. REG: CI fails if pubspec.yaml and the committed lockfile disagree (`pub get --enforce-lockfile` or a dry-run diff step).
2. Name the exact parent dep that newly pulls flutter_inappwebview (`dart pub deps` on a fresh resolve vs the last green nightly) and constrain it (pin upper bound) — or, if the plugin is genuinely unneeded, exclude it at the source.
3. Decide policy for the plugin's native legs regardless: linux leg either installs libwpewebkit-1.0-dev in the workflow or drops the plugin; windows leg either pins the older toolset or bumps to an inappwebview version with cppwinrt coroutines.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: nightly linux + windows release builds green.
- AC2: flutter_app/pubspec.lock committed and enforced in CI (AC of the REG guard).
- AC3: the parent dep + the version that introduced the drift is named in this issue (data, not vibes).

Unassigned per owner.

# Rework — gh-1265 (PR #1268): red Quality gate on head `a702c3170`

## Issues/Notes

- **CI failure (Quality gate)**: the aggregate Quality gate went red on head `a702c3170dde9b168e645a57e1cf6b9eb68869fc`. The full CI log was not attached (`ci_failures_full.log` missing), so the failing leg was identified by local reproduction.
- **Root cause (reproduced locally)**: merge commit `a702c3170` brought `chore(release): v1.0.513` in from `main`, bumping the root `pubspec.yaml` (and `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`) to `1.0.513` — but the **committed `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` still recorded the `flutter_agent_harness` path dependency at `1.0.511`**. Every `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` step this PR added then exits 1:

  ```text
  Would change 1 dependency.
  Unable to satisfy `pubspec.yaml` using `pubspec.lock`.
  ```

  The first flutter_app pub-get step in any CI leg (e.g. `static`, `flutter-analyze`, `flutter-tests`, …) fails → aggregate Quality gate fails. This is exactly the skew class the PR's own AC2 REG guard was designed to catch — the merge from `main` introduced it after the lockfile was committed.
- **Not a previous-attempt repeat**: this is a new failure mode (lockfile/pubspec version skew from the main merge), not the nightly desktop legs the PR originally fixed — those remain green locally (guard test AC1/AC3 pass, linux release build verified in the PR).

## Approach

TDD (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR) against the concrete CI failure:

1. **RED** — added a test to `test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` (AC2 group): the committed lockfile's recorded root-package version must equal `pubspec.yaml`'s version, and `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`'s version must not lag the root version. With the stale lockfile restored this fails exactly as CI did: `Expected: 1.0.513 / Actual: 1.0.511` (13 passed, 1 failed).
2. **GREEN** — regenerated the lockfile (`cd flutter_app && flutter pub get`; single-line change `1.0.511` → `1.0.513` for the path dep). `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` now succeeds and the guard test passes **14/14**.
3. **REFACTOR** — none needed; the fix is one lockfile line plus the regression test.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` | Regenerated: `flutter_agent_harness` path dep `1.0.511` → `1.0.513` (sync with the v1.0.513 release bump from main). |
| `test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` | New AC2 test `lockfile is in sync with the current package versions` — fails if a future merge/release chore bumps versions without regenerating the committed lockfile, so this breaks locally instead of red-lighting every CI leg. |

(Committed as `0aff6c34e` — new head for validation.)

## Test Coverage

- **Guard test**: `dart test test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` → **14/14 pass** (was 13/14 RED before the lockfile regen). `dart analyze` on the file: no issues.
- **Enforce-lockfile verification**: `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile --directory=flutter_app` now succeeds (exits 0); previously exited 1 with "Unable to satisfy pubspec.yaml using pubspec.lock".
- **Skew sweep**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` is the only committed lockfile in the repo (`git ls-files`), so no other lockfile can carry the same skew; all remaining `flutter pub get` occurrences in workflows are either `--enforce-lockfile` or non-flutter_app library steps (left as-is intentionally).
- **Full suite**: `dart test` ran to completion with all tests passing, but the Dart VM hit a **pre-existing native shutdown crash in this sandbox** (`tcache_thread_shutdown(): unaligned tcache chunk detected / Aborted`) *after* the final test — reproduced with a minimal subset (`dart test test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_attach_test.dart test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` → "🎉 22 tests passed" then the same abort at VM exit). The crash is environmental (VM shutdown), unrelated to this change, which touches zero runtime code (one lockfile version line + a text/YAML guard test).

## Notes

- The open PR "thread" is a top-level bot comment (`threadId`/`rootCommentId` are `null` in `pr_discussions_raw.json`), not an inline review thread — no threaded replies are required (`outputs/review_replies.json` is `{ "replies": [] }`).
- AC1 (windows leg) remains verified by symmetry as stated in the PR description — no Windows host available; the stub mechanism is proven on linux.

# --- Vendored interpreter runtimes for the run_script tool (offscreen
# document). Extension CSP forbids remote scripts — these ship in-bundle. ---
"$(dirname "$0")/vendor_interpreters.sh"

# --- Embedded agent (dart2js). Output is a build artifact: never committed. ---
agent_js=browser_ext/sw/agent.js
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "building embedded agent (dart2js)…"
  ( cd browser_ext/dart \
    && dart pub get >/dev/null \
    && dart compile js -O2 -o ../sw/agent.js agent_main.dart )
  rm -f "${agent_js}.deps" "${agent_js}.map"
elif [ -f "$agent_js" ]; then
  echo "dart SDK not found — shipping prebuilt $agent_js"
else
  echo "WARNING: no dart SDK and no prebuilt sw/agent.js — scaffold-only zip (embedded agent disabled)"
fi

# --- Optional fa web app (flutter_app → browser_ext/app). Build artifact. ---
if [ "$with_app" -eq 1 ]; then
  if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: --with-app passed but flutter is not installed — cannot build browser_ext/app/" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
  # --base-href MUST match the panel-relative location: panel.js resolves
  # 'app/index.html' against panel/panel.html, so the bundle lives at
  # browser_ext/panel/app/ (a root-level copy is invisible to the panel).
  ( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null
    # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (pubspec.yaml),
    # so the web build dies bundling it when the file is absent (#140).
    # Create it AFTER pub get — pub get removes a placeholder touched
    # earlier (runs 34593431895, 34596707238) — and keep it non-empty:
    # the populated placeholder is the shape build-macos.yml's app job
    # has shipped green. A real local .env (developer keys) is never
    # overwritten.
----
# --- 3. The fa web app (flutter_app → outlook/app) — MANDATORY. ---
if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: flutter is not installed — cannot build outlook/app/" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
# --base-href MUST match the taskpane URL: the pane opens
# /outlook/app/index.html directly (manifest 1.2.0.0), so the bundle
# lives at build/pages/root/outlook/app/.
( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null && \
  FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/ \
  flutter build web --release --pwa-strategy=none --base-href=/outlook/app/ \
    --dart-define=FA_HOST=office )
rm -rf "$out/app"
mkdir -p "$out/app"
cp -R flutter_app/build/web/. "$out/app/"
# Vendored WASI interpreter assets are mobile-only (#1096 AC3): loaded
# exclusively through WasiSandboxShell (env_factory_io.dart — Android/iOS);
# the web pane compiles env_factory_stub (wasm_run needs dart:ffi) and
# runs python/js/sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net (web_interpreters_web.dart).
# ~47MB that never loads in the browser — drop from the bundle.

Found a real gap: `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:68` and `scripts/build_office_addin.sh:54` each run `cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null` (no --enforce-lockfile), and both scripts ARE invoked in CI workflows (browser-ext.yml:147, build-macos.yml:927, office-addin.yml:101, pages.yml:96,107). In those workflows, the preceding explicit `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` step usually runs first... but not always:

- browser-ext.yml:147: the step right before runs `(cd flutter_app && flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile)` (from the diff at line 143-146). So by the time the script runs, deps are already resolved and `flutter pub get` inside the script is a no-op success. Same for pages.yml:96 (line 50 step enforces first). build-macos.yml:927 — is there a prior flutter_app pub get in that job? Need to check. office-addin.yml:101 — the Office wiring step at line 94 runs enforce-lockfile before... but that's `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile && flutter test`. If that step is in the same job before line 101, the resolution is already done, and the script's plain `flutter pub get` is a no-op.

However: `flutter pub get` (plain) when lockfile and pubspec are in sync does nothing and exits 0 — it doesn't rewrite the lockfile. So in practice it's benign in CI when a prior enforce step ran. But if the ordering changes or the script is invoked standalone in a workflow without a prior enforce step, it would float. This is the class of drift the PR is trying to kill; the scripts' internal pub get is a hole. Severity: the guard test only checks workflow YAML steps, not these script invocations. It's a real maintainability/consistency gap → IMPORTANT (not blocking, since currently a prior enforce step precedes each invocation... let me verify build-macos.yml:927 context and office-addin.yml:101 context).

Replaces the hosted `flutter_inappwebview_linux` (0.1.0-beta.1) via
`dependency_overrides` in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`.

- **What this is**: a same-name, same-version stub with an empty Dart lib
  and **no `flutter: plugin:` section**.
- **Why**: the umbrella `flutter_inappwebview: 6.2.0-beta.3` (direct dep
  since gh-1235) pulls this implementation into every linux build, and its
  native CMake hard-requires the WPE WebKit system library
  (`CMakeLists.txt:63` — nightly linux release leg red 5 nights,
  10-01 → 10-05). `libwpewebkit-1.0-dev` does not exist on Ubuntu 24.04
  (noble; verified against packages.ubuntu.com — jammy-only), so the
  plugin cannot be built on `ubuntu-latest` at all.
- **Why it's safe**: the app never uses flutter_inappwebview on Linux —
  `createFaWebViewHost()` returns null there (renderer placeholder). With
  no plugin registration, `flutter build linux --release` compiles none of
  the plugin's C++ and the app is functionally unchanged.
- **Dropping the stub**: delete the `dependency_overrides` entry in
  flutter_app/pubspec.yaml and this directory, then regenerate
  flutter_app/pubspec.lock — but only once the linux leg can satisfy the
  WPE WebKit requirement (new runner image, upstream making the dependency
  optional, or upstream shipping a linux impl without it).

With `channel: stable`, when a new Flutter stable releases with a higher Dart SDK, `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` checks lockfile SDK constraints: the lockfile sdks section records the lower bounds. Enforce-lockfile fails if "the current Dart/Flutter SDK doesn't satisfy the lockfile's sdk constraints"? Actually the sdks section in the lockfile records the constraints derived at resolution time, not upper bounds. A newer SDK satisfies `>=3.13.0 <4.0.0` fine. But there's a nuance: if the new Flutter stable bumps packages' SDK constraints such that the locked versions no longer satisfy... enforce-lockfile only checks that resolution from the lockfile is still valid, not that it's the latest. Locked versions remain valid if their SDK constraints are satisfied by the new SDK — newer SDK satisfies old constraints. It doesn't fail merely because newer package versions exist. However, if a dependency requires an upper bound like `<3.14.0`... unlikely. So mostly OK.

Bigger question: does `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` fail when the Flutter SDK version differs from the one that generated the lockfile? No — it fails only if the lockfile is not consistent with pubspec.yaml. SDK constraints recorded in the lockfile are minimum bounds; a newer stable satisfies them. So stable-floating workflows are fine unless a new stable breaks a locked package's environment (then that would be a genuine issue to catch anyway... actually it would fail the build, which is arguably good — pin the SDK).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,

## gh-1265 — nightly linux/windows release legs red: unused `flutter_inappwebview` desktop impls + uncommitted lockfile

### Root Cause
- gh-1235's **direct** `flutter_inappwebview: ^6.2.0-beta.3` dep pulls the umbrella's desktop implementations (`flutter_inappwebview_linux 0.1.0-beta.1`, `flutter_inappwebview_windows 0.7.0-beta.3`) into every native desktop build — the ticket's "transitive, nobody declares it" theory is stale (verified: `js_widget_runtime`, hosted 0.4.155 AND git bd1e7c2, declares no inappwebview; the umbrella is the only graph edge).
- Linux: the plugin's CMake hard-requires WPE WebKit; `libwpewebkit-1.0-dev` **does not exist on Ubuntu 24.04** (jammy-only, verified) — reproduced locally: `flutter build linux --release` → the exact `CMakeLists.txt:63` error.
- Windows: plugin C++17 sources (no `/await`) include `<experimental/coroutine>` via cppwinrt → MSVC 14.51 STL1011; no published version fixes it.
- The app never uses the plugin on Linux/Windows (`createFaWebViewHost()` returns null there → placeholder), and `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` was gitignored, so the drift hit CI as a 5-night mystery.

### Fix
- `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` + `vendor/flutter_inappwebview_{linux,windows}_stub/`: same-name stub overrides with **no** `flutter: plugin:` section (mirrors the existing `vendor/flutter_inappwebview_macos` pattern) — desktop builds compile zero inappwebview C++; `VENDORED.md` documents drop conditions.
- `.gitignore`: `!flutter_app/pubspec.lock` negation (after every `pubspec.lock` rule — the file has a duplicated block); `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` committed (umbrella 6.2.0-beta.3 pinned).
- All 7 workflows' flutter_app pub-get steps → `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` (ci, nightly, build-mobile, build-macos, browser-ext, office-addin, pages) — skew now fails CI instead of floating.
- Stale pubspec comments updated; `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/linux/wasm_run-*/` gitignored (linux-build download cache swept into the branch during verification, removed).

### Test Coverage
- **RED**: `test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` — 12 of 13 failed before the fix (13/13 pass after): lockfile committed/not-ignored, per-workflow enforce-lockfile, stub overrides carry no plugin section, drift chain pinned (AC3 data in code), nightly still exercises linux+windows.
- Local: linux repro (WPE error) → green `flutter build linux --release` with stubs, bundle contains no inappwebview native lib; `--enforce-lockfile` passes in sync and exits 1 on skew.
- Full suite: **9013 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures**; `dart analyze` clean (pre-existing infos only).

### Notes
- **AC3**: parent dep = `flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 (direct, gh-1235) → `_linux 0.1.0-beta.1` (new WPE system-lib requirement) + `_windows 0.7.0-beta.3` (C++17-without-/await sources).
- **Windows leg** (AC1) is verified by symmetry, not executed: no Windows host available. The stub removes the plugin from the windows build graph (registrant regenerated, CMake plugin list updated — same mechanism proven on linux), returning the leg to the exact native surface it had when green on 09-30. First nightly run should confirm.
- `flutter pub get` prints a benign warning that the umbrella's `default_package` refs are "not a plugin package" — expected, that is the stub doing its job.
- The windows runner stays `windows-latest` (no toolset pin needed once the plugin C++ is out of the build).

# gh-1265: [BUG] nightly red 5 nights: native desktop builds broken by a TRANSITIVE flutter_inappwebview nobody declares — linux WPE missing + windows MSVC 14.51 STL1011 (lockfile not committed)

## Description

**Evidence** (nightly run 37260378075, red every night 10-01 → 10-05):
- Build linux (release): `flutter_inappwebview_linux/linux/CMakeLists.txt:63: WPE WebKit not found. Please install libwpewebkit-1.0-dev`
- Build windows (release): `MSVC 14.51 (VS 18) include/experimental/coroutine(37,1): error C2338 STL1011: The /await…` from `flutter_inappwebview_windows` sources (legacy coroutine-TS header rejected by the runner image's new toolchain).

**Root cause (verified on origin/main): NO pubspec or committed lockfile mentions flutter_inappwebview, and zero Dart code references it** — it arrives as a fresh TRANSITIVE resolution on CI: flutter_app/pubspec.lock is not committed, so nightly's `pub get` floats to the latest compatible versions; some caret dep released in the last ~5 days now pulls flutter_inappwebview, and its native legs break both desktop builds (linux: new system-lib requirement; windows: plugin code incompatible with the updated MSVC).

**Fix (layered):**
1. **Commit flutter_app/pubspec.lock** (app, not library — lockfile belongs in git) so CI builds are reproducible and transitive drift surfaces as a deliberate PR diff, not a 5-red-nights mystery. REG: CI fails if pubspec.yaml and the committed lockfile disagree (`pub get --enforce-lockfile` or a dry-run diff step).
2. Name the exact parent dep that newly pulls flutter_inappwebview (`dart pub deps` on a fresh resolve vs the last green nightly) and constrain it (pin upper bound) — or, if the plugin is genuinely unneeded, exclude it at the source.
3. Decide policy for the plugin's native legs regardless: linux leg either installs libwpewebkit-1.0-dev in the workflow or drops the plugin; windows leg either pins the older toolset or bumps to an inappwebview version with cppwinrt coroutines.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: nightly linux + windows release builds green.
- AC2: flutter_app/pubspec.lock committed and enforced in CI (AC of the REG guard).
- AC3: the parent dep + the version that introduced the drift is named in this issue (data, not vibes).

# --- Vendored interpreter runtimes for the run_script tool (offscreen
# document). Extension CSP forbids remote scripts — these ship in-bundle. ---
"$(dirname "$0")/vendor_interpreters.sh"

# --- Embedded agent (dart2js). Output is a build artifact: never committed. ---
agent_js=browser_ext/sw/agent.js
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "building embedded agent (dart2js)…"
  ( cd browser_ext/dart \
    && dart pub get >/dev/null \
    && dart compile js -O2 -o ../sw/agent.js agent_main.dart )
  rm -f "${agent_js}.deps" "${agent_js}.map"
elif [ -f "$agent_js" ]; then
  echo "dart SDK not found — shipping prebuilt $agent_js"
else
  echo "WARNING: no dart SDK and no prebuilt sw/agent.js — scaffold-only zip (embedded agent disabled)"
fi

# --- Optional fa web app (flutter_app → browser_ext/app). Build artifact. ---
if [ "$with_app" -eq 1 ]; then
  if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: --with-app passed but flutter is not installed — cannot build browser_ext/app/" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
  # --base-href MUST match the panel-relative location: panel.js resolves
  # 'app/index.html' against panel/panel.html, so the bundle lives at
  # browser_ext/panel/app/ (a root-level copy is invisible to the panel).
  ( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null
    # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (pubspec.yaml),
    # so the web build dies bundling it when the file is absent (#140).
    # Create it AFTER pub get — pub get removes a placeholder touched
    # earlier (runs 34593431895, 34596707238) — and keep it non-empty:
    # the populated placeholder is the shape build-macos.yml's app job
    # has shipped green. A real local .env (developer keys) is never
    # overwritten.
----
# --- 3. The fa web app (flutter_app → outlook/app) — MANDATORY. ---
if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: flutter is not installed — cannot build outlook/app/" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
# --base-href MUST match the taskpane URL: the pane opens
# /outlook/app/index.html directly (manifest 1.2.0.0), so the bundle
# lives at build/pages/root/outlook/app/.
( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null && \
  FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/ \
  flutter build web --release --pwa-strategy=none --base-href=/outlook/app/ \
    --dart-define=FA_HOST=office )
rm -rf "$out/app"
mkdir -p "$out/app"
cp -R flutter_app/build/web/. "$out/app/"
# Vendored WASI interpreter assets are mobile-only (#1096 AC3): loaded
# exclusively through WasiSandboxShell (env_factory_io.dart — Android/iOS);
# the web pane compiles env_factory_stub (wasm_run needs dart:ffi) and
# runs python/js/sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net (web_interpreters_web.dart).
# ~47MB that never loads in the browser — drop from the bundle.

In those workflows, the preceding explicit `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` step usually runs first... but not always:

So by the time the script runs, deps are already resolved and `flutter pub get` inside the script is a no-op success. However: `flutter pub get` (plain) when lockfile and pubspec are in sync does nothing and exits 0 — it doesn't rewrite the lockfile. So in practice it's benign in CI when a prior enforce step ran. But if the ordering changes or the script is invoked standalone in a workflow without a prior enforce step, it would float. This is the class of drift the PR is trying to kill; the scripts' internal pub get is a hole. Severity: the guard test only checks workflow YAML steps, not these script invocations. Replaces the hosted `flutter_inappwebview_linux` (0.1.0-beta.1) via
`dependency_overrides` in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`.

- **What this is**: a same-name, same-version stub with an empty Dart lib
  and **no `flutter: plugin:` section**.
- **Why**: the umbrella `flutter_inappwebview: 6.2.0-beta.3` (direct dep
  since gh-1235) pulls this implementation into every linux build, and its
  native CMake hard-requires the WPE WebKit system library
  (`CMakeLists.txt:63` — nightly linux release leg red 5 nights,
  10-01 → 10-05). `libwpewebkit-1.0-dev` does not exist on Ubuntu 24.04
  (noble; verified against packages.ubuntu.com — jammy-only), so the
  plugin cannot be built on `ubuntu-latest` at all.
- **Why it's safe**: the app never uses flutter_inappwebview on Linux —
  `createFaWebViewHost()` returns null there (renderer placeholder). With
  no plugin registration, `flutter build linux --release` compiles none of
  the plugin's C++ and the app is functionally unchanged.
- **Dropping the stub**: delete the `dependency_overrides` entry in
  flutter_app/pubspec.yaml and this directory, then regenerate
  flutter_app/pubspec.lock — but only once the linux leg can satisfy the
  WPE WebKit requirement (new runner image, upstream making the dependency
  optional, or upstream shipping a linux impl without it).

With `channel: stable`, when a new Flutter stable releases with a higher Dart SDK, `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` checks lockfile SDK constraints: the lockfile sdks section records the lower bounds. Enforce-lockfile fails if "the current Dart/Flutter SDK doesn't satisfy the lockfile's sdk constraints"? Actually the sdks section in the lockfile records the constraints derived at resolution time, not upper bounds. A newer SDK satisfies `>=3.13.0 <4.0.0` fine. But there's a nuance: if the new Flutter stable bumps packages' SDK constraints such that the locked versions no longer satisfy... enforce-lockfile only checks that resolution from the lockfile is still valid, not that it's the latest. Locked versions remain valid if their SDK constraints are satisfied by the new SDK — newer SDK satisfies old constraints. It doesn't fail merely because newer package versions exist. However, if a dependency requires an upper bound like `<3.14.0`... unlikely. So mostly OK.

Bigger question: does `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` fail when the Flutter SDK version differs from the one that generated the lockfile? No — it fails only if the lockfile is not consistent with pubspec.yaml. SDK constraints recorded in the lockfile are minimum bounds; a newer stable satisfies them. So stable-floating workflows are fine unless a new stable breaks a locked package's environment (then that would be a genuine issue to catch anyway... actually it would fail the build, which is arguably good — pin the SDK).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
